In brief: Abuja is expected to experience a week of warm and humid conditions with a high chance of rainfall, with temperature highs ranging from 27 to 29 degrees Celsius and rainfall accumulation ranges varying between 10 to 30 millimeters per day. The current weather conditions in Abuja are characterized by a temperature of 23 degrees Celsius, which feels like 26 degrees Celsius due to the high humidity of 94 percent. The wind is blowing at a moderate speed of 13 kilometers per hour, and the UV index is at a moderate level of 4. As we look ahead to the week, models suggest that a low-pressure system will develop over the region, leading to an increase in rainfall activity. My best guess is that the system will move eastwards, bringing with it a high chance of rainfall on Monday and Tuesday.
### Monday The low-pressure system is expected to dominate the weather pattern on Monday, with a high chance of rainfall of 85 percent. The rain is likely to start in the late morning, around 10 am, and will continue throughout the day, with the heaviest downpour expected in the late afternoon. The temperature will rise to a high of 29 degrees Celsius, but the feels-like temperature will be higher due to the high humidity. The wind will be blowing at a speed of 15 kilometers per hour, which will help to distribute the heat and make the conditions feel more bearable. In areas such as Maitama and Garki, the rain will be more intense, with accumulation ranges of up to 25 millimeters per hour. The rainfall will have a significant impact on the traffic, especially on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway, where the speed is already reduced due to the road construction. The airport road will also be affected, with a high chance of flooding in the low-lying areas. Residents living in flood-prone areas such as Gwarinpa should be prepared for possible flooding, with a high chance of water accumulation on the roads and in the homes. The humidity will remain high throughout the day, at an average of 90 percent, which will make the conditions feel hot and sticky. The rain will start to clear up in the evening, around 6 pm, and the temperature will drop to a low of 22 degrees Celsius. The wind will die down, and the conditions will become calm, with a clear sky and a low UV index. This will be a welcome relief for residents, especially those living in areas such as Wuse, where the heat and humidity have been intense.

The rain will be more scattered on Tuesday, with the heaviest downpour expected in the late morning. The conditions will be cloudy, with a high cloud cover, and the UV index will be low. In areas such as Aso Rock and the National Assembly, the rain will be lighter, with accumulation ranges of up to 10 millimeters per hour. The humidity will remain high, at an average of 85 percent, but it will be lower than on Monday. This will be a good time for residents to engage in outdoor activities, such as walking or jogging, especially in areas such as the Three Arms Zone.
